requested.title: Production promotion executes a mutable GitHub Action tag

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The current workflow fully retains `uses: actions/checkout@v5` as the first step of the privileged `promote` job. `v5` is a movable Git tag, not an immutable full commit SHA, so GitHub resolves the action implementation at execution time from a mutable reference. The workflow-level permissions grant `contents: write`, and the `promote` job does not narrow them; therefore its automatic GitHub token can modify repository contents and the `production` branch. The job also targets the `cloud-production` environment, so any environment secrets approved for that job are available to code executing in the job. A compromised or retargeted upstream `actions/checkout` v5 action would execute before the workflow validates `inputs.sha`, successful CI, ancestry, or deployment status. `persist-credentials: false` only prevents checkout from leaving credentials in local Git configuration; it does not prevent the action itself from receiving or accessing its default token during execution. Git history shows later changes added review inputs, a private-test exception, and authenticated fetches, but none replaced the mutable checkout tag with a commit SHA. Consequently, an upstream action compromise provides a concrete pre-validation supply-chain path to exfiltrate available credentials or use the write-scoped token to alter the repository.
